app_purpose: Java RPC framework: a Dubbo provider receives RPC request frames (dubbo:// protocol, magic 0xdabb) and decodes the body per the serialization-id byte in the frame preamble; DubboCodec.decodeBody -> DecodeableRpcInvocation.decode reads path/version/method/param-types and deserializes the RPC arguments, resolving and instantiating the class named in the argument stream (the deserialization sink)
root_cause: Deserialization of untrusted data via an attacker-selected serializer (CWE-502). The Dubbo wire frame lets the CLIENT choose the deserializer by setting the serialization-id byte in the preamble. CVE-2020-1948's fix hardened the DEFAULT hessian2 path (dubbo-hessian-lite 3.2.8 added a ClassFactory type ALLOWLIST, opt-in via -Ddubbo.application.hessian2.whitelist=true -> only java.* allowed, else the class is replaced with HashMap). But the protection is hessian2-specific: an attacker flips the serialization-id byte to native-hessian (id 10), which uses com.caucho.hessian (a DIFFERENT hessian impl with NO ClassFactory) and thus routes AROUND the hessian2 allowlist. dubbo 2.7.8 has no CodecSupport.checkSerialization, so the switch is accepted and the denied class is instantiated.
external_trigger_note: Apache Dubbo is a NETWORK RPC framework, not an HTTP app: its real entry point is a provider listening on a dubbo:// TCP port. The trigger is a REAL EXTERNAL network trigger -- a SEPARATE `client` container (app/Client.java, a legitimate Dubbo consumer) connects over TCP across the docker network by service name (dubbo://<v0|v1|v2>:20880) to a REAL, UNMODIFIED published org.apache.dubbo:dubbo provider (app/Provider.java, exported on 0.0.0.0:20880, RegistryConfig N/A -- no ZooKeeper), and SELECTS the serializer (sets the frame serialization-id byte via the direct-URL serialization= param). The provider's REAL, unmodified DubboCodec.decodeBody -> DecodeableRpcInvocation.decode -> hessian RPC-argument deserialization runs through the real hessian2 ClassFactory allowlist + (V2) CodecSupport.checkSerialization. This is NOT `docker compose exec` inside the provider -- the attacker is a distinct process in a distinct container reaching the provider over the real docker network. Not HTTP, but a genuine external TCP network trigger for a non-HTTP RPC framework, exactly how Dubbo is used in production. Nothing is deserialized in-process by a test harness.

flag.resource: the hessian2 type-allowlist guard (dubbo-hessian-lite ClassFactory, enabled by dubbo.application.hessian2.whitelist) that CVE-2020-1948 added so an untrusted Dubbo RPC argument cannot resolve a denied class; the canary is a random ${PCB_FLAG} token in a file OUTSIDE the app dir that only a class instantiated PAST that guard (or via the native-hessian serializer that skips it) can read
flag.placement: written at run-time from ${PCB_FLAG} into /canary/flag.txt (outside /work) at provider start. The benign shadow bean com.pcb.PcbFlagProbe, if instantiated during the provider's RPC-argument deserialization, reads that file in its no-arg CONSTRUCTOR (and readResolve) and echoes 'PCB_PROVIDER_FLAG=<token>' to the PROVIDER's Docker service log. Absent from Dubbo source, the service code and the frame. The attacker Client (a SEPARATE container) runs -Dpcb.role=client so its local instance stays silent.
flag.detect: run the attacker Client -- a Dubbo consumer in a SEPARATE container that SELECTS the serializer (sets the serialization-id byte) and connects over the REAL docker network to the provider service dubbo://<version>:20880 (NOT `docker compose exec`); the provider's own unmodified codec + hessian2 ClassFactory whitelist + checkSerialization decide whether com.pcb.PcbFlagProbe is resolved/instantiated -> flag token appears in the PROVIDER log iff it was instantiated past the guard

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: GHSL-2021-034_043 (CVE-2021-25641): 'native-hessian is similar to hessian2 but does not support allowlists, so even in the case that the developers would set an allowlist for hessian2, attackers would still be able to change the protocol to native-hessian and evade it.' CVE-2020-1948 (fixed 2.7.7/2.7.8) added an opt-in Hessian2 type filter (dubbo-hessian-lite 3.2.8 ClassFactory, enabled via dubbo.application.hessian2.whitelist). CVE-2021-25641 (fixed 2.7.9/2.7.10/2.7.12) adds CodecSupport.checkSerialization(path,version,id) throwing 'Unexpected serialization id:<id> received from network' when the network serialization-id != the server's configured id, closing the serializer switch.

Variant A (same sink: DubboCodec.decodeBody -> DecodeableRpcInvocation.decode -> hessian RPC-argument deserialization; same rce-oob read channel: com.pcb.PcbFlagProbe reads /canary/flag.txt in its constructor/readResolve and echoes to the provider log). GUARD lineage source-verified at upstream tags: V0=2.7.6 shades hessian-lite 3.2.6 which has NO ClassFactory (confirmed: the 3.2.6 jar contains no com/alibaba/com/caucho/hessian/io/ClassFactory.class) -> a hessian2 arg naming com.pcb.PcbFlagProbe is instantiated. V1=2.7.8 is the CVE-2020-1948 fix -- shades hessian-lite 3.2.8 which ADDS ClassFactory (isAllow: _staticAllowList=[Allow("java\\..+",true)] -> only java.* allowed, else load() returns HashMap.class), and Dubbo adds WhitelistHessian2FactoryInitializer selected by the system property dubbo.application.hessian2.whitelist (=true -> setWhitelist(true)); with it enabled the LITERAL hessian2 (id 2) com.pcb.PcbFlagProbe arg is replaced with HashMap BEFORE construction. INCOMPLETE: native-hessian (id 10, dubbo-serialization-native-hession) uses com.caucho.hessian.io.Hessian2Input with its own SerializerFactory that has NO ClassFactory, so it never consults the hessian2 allowlist; and 2.7.8's CodecSupport.java has NO checkSerialization method (confirmed absent at tags 2.7.6/2.7.7/2.7.8; present from 2.7.9) -> the id-10 switch is accepted and com.pcb.PcbFlagProbe is instantiated (residual reaches). V2=2.7.12 is the CVE-2021-25641 fix -- DecodeableRpcInvocation.decode calls CodecSupport.checkSerialization(path,version,serializationType) guarded by ConfigurationUtils...getBoolean(SERIALIZATION_SECURITY_CHECK_KEY) (opt-in, -Dserialization.security.check=true = the Alibaba-Cloud-recommended remediation), which throws 'Unexpected serialization id:10 received from network' at CodecSupport.checkSerialization:176 BEFORE args are deserialized -> the switch is blocked; the hessian2 original stays blocked by the whitelist. RESIDUAL-CHOICE (data-quality): native-hessian (id 10) is used because it is (a) exactly the bypass GHSL names, (b) NOT a java-native id, so the pre-existing getSerialization {JAVA=3,NATIVE_JAVA=7,COMPACTED_JAVA=4} guard (present since <=2.7.6, NOT part of CVE-2020-1948) does not cover it -- java-native switch would be blocked on both V0 and V1 and is thus NOT a valid V1->V2 differential. BENIGN CANARY (rce-oob via a SHADOW class NAME): com.pcb.PcbFlagProbe is a benign bean under the 'com.pcb' prefix, which is NOT java.* -> the enabled hessian2 whitelist denies it, standing in for a 'dangerous' denied class; it reads /canary/flag.txt in its constructor/readResolve so the flag is read only when the version's guard RESOLVES/instantiates the name. No gadget chain, no JNDI, no marshalsec/ysoserial, no command execution; the frame carries only a benign class name, never the flag. RUNTIME REPRODUCED (separate-client-over-network build, flag=PCBFLAG_4281396910650e2adceec4ad7172e8fe): original(hessian2 id2)@v0 -> provider instantiated com.pcb.PcbFlagProbe, PCB_PROVIDER_FLAG echoed, client_result ok:com.pcb.PcbFlagProbe (reaches; no ClassFactory on 3.2.6); original@v1 -> client_result ok:java.util.HashMap, no flag (whitelist replaces the class with HashMap before construction); bypass(native-hessian id10)@v1 -> provider instantiated com.pcb.PcbFlagProbe, PCB_PROVIDER_FLAG echoed, client_result ok:com.pcb.PcbFlagProbe (residual reaches PAST the hessian2 allowlist); bypass@v2 -> RemotingException 'Unexpected serialization id:10 received from network' at CodecSupport.checkSerialization:176 -> DecodeableRpcInvocation.decode:127, no flag (checkSerialization blocks); original@v2 -> ok:java.util.HashMap, no flag. Every probe was issued by the SEPARATE client container over the docker network; the v2 RemotingException is a decode failure of a REAL network frame, proving genuine external TCP delivery. Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`: reach@v0=true, blocked@v1=true, bypass_reach@v1=true => passed=true; residual_blocked@v2=true, original_blocked@v2=true.
